ety.text: Inherited from Middle English gap /gappe, from Old Norse gap (“an empty space, gap, chasm”), from gapa (“to gape, scream”), from Proto-Germanic *gapōną, from Proto-Indo-European *ǵʰeh₂- (“to open wide, gape”). Related to Danish gab (“an expanse, space, gap”), Old English ġeap (“open space, expanse”). Doublet of gape.
A variant of gape.

senses.d: An opening in anything, made by breaking or parting.
ex: He made a gap in the fence by kicking at a weak spot.

senses.d: An opening allowing passage or entrance.
ex: We can slip through that gap between the buildings.

senses.d: An opening that implies a breach or defect.
ex: There is a gap between the roof and the gutter.
I have a gap in my schedule next Tuesday.

senses.d: A hiatus, a pause in something which is otherwise continuous.
ex: I'm taking a gap.
You must wait for a gap in the traffic before crossing the road.

senses.d: A vacancy, deficit, absence, or lack.
ex: Their departure has left a gap in the workforce.
Find words to fill the gaps in an incomplete sentence.
The exploring party went through the high gap in the mountains.

senses.d: A sheltered area of coast between two cliffs (mostly restricted to place names).
ex: At Birling Gap we can stop and go have a picnic on the beach.
Jones doubled through the gap.

senses.d: The shortfall between the amount the medical insurer will pay to the service provider and the scheduled fee for the item.
ex: Under bulk billing the patient does not pay a gap, and the medical practitioner receives 85% of the scheduled fee.

senses.d: To notch, as a sword or knife.
To make an opening in; to breach.
To check the size of a gap.
ex: I gapped all the spark plugs in my car, but then realized I had used the wrong manual and had made them too small.

senses.d: To surpass (someone or something) by a considerable margin.
ex: Honestly K&C could release today with like a bit more SOT buffs and they'd probably still gap a lot of the game

senses.d: To fall or spill open so as to leave a gap.
ex: The robe gaps open at the waist, breasts spilling out of a lacy bra that looks like she might have had it since her college days.

senses.d: Of an electric train, to be positioned, or to cause to be positioned, between electrical pickup points, causing loss of power.
ex: The lights flickered as the train momentarily gapped.
The train was gapped just outside the station, and passengers were stranded for nearly two hours.
